THE DOMINION BUREAU OF STATISTICS ON YMCA CAMPING, 1938-1946
Canada, Department of Trade and Commerce, Dominion Bureau of Statistics,
Education Statistics Branch: "Elementary and Secondary Education in Canada",
being Part I of the BIENNIAL SURVEY OF EDUCATION IN CANADA.
Internet Archive item 31761119680775. Fully downloadable, 4.05 MB of text.
Read 2026-09-07.

=====================================================================
FIRST, WHAT THE ITEM ACTUALLY IS -- BECAUSE THE TITLE PAGE LIES BY OMISSION
=====================================================================

The title page reads "ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY EDUCATION IN CANADA, 1936-38 /
Published by Authority of the Hon. W. D. Euler, M.P., Minister of Trade and
Commerce / Ottawa: J. O. Patenaude, Printer to the King's Most Excellent
Majesty / 1940 / Price, 50 cents."

IT IS A BOUND RUN OF AT LEAST TWELVE SURVEYS. Interior title pages carry
1936-38, 1938-40, 1940-42, 1943-44, 1944-46, 1945-46, 1947-48, 1948-50,
1950-54, 1954-56 and 1956-58. This is the second bound-run item found in one
day, after the religious-education yearbooks, and the same discipline applies:
place every occurrence by the interior title page above it, not by the item's.

=====================================================================
THE ENTRY, VERBATIM, FROM THE 1938-40 SURVEY
=====================================================================

Under "SOME NATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS", between the Victorian Order of Nurses and
a list of Empire and international bodies:

  "Young Men's Christian Association of Canada.--First organized in Canada in
  1851, have two active boys' programmes in co-operation with schools, namely,
  Hi-Y clubs for older high school boys and Gra-Y clubs for younger boys in
  public or grade schools. THE Y.M.C.A. HAS CONDUCTED ORGANIZED BOYS' CAMPS
  SINCE 1889 and is particularly concerned with THE EDUCATIONAL ASPECTS OF
  CAMPING. Nelson McEwen on the National Council of Y.M.C.A. of Canada, 21
  Dundas Street, Toronto, is the chief boys' work director."

THE SAME ENTRY APPEARS IN THE 1943-44 AND 1945-46 SURVEYS, nearly word for
word. The differences are small and they are the point:

  1938-40   "21 Dundas STREET"    "chief boys' work DIRECTOR"
  1943-44   "21 Dundas SQUARE"    "chief boys' work SECRETARY"
  1945-46   "21 Dundas SQUARE"    "chief boys' work SECRETARY"   ("has two"
                                   for "have two", one comma moved)

=====================================================================
HOW MUCH WEIGHT IT WILL BEAR, WHICH IS LESS THAN IT LOOKS
=====================================================================

THIS IS STANDING BOILERPLATE, NOT THREE INDEPENDENT ATTESTATIONS. The
paragraph is reprinted survey after survey with only an address and a job
title touched up, which is what an entry supplied once by the organization
itself and lightly re-checked looks like. So:

  * The 1889 date is ONE claim printed three times, not three witnesses.
  * McEwen's tenure is attested at each printing only as far as the Bureau
    bothered to re-check it, and the evidence that they re-checked at all is
    that "Street" became "Square" and "director" became "secretary".

WHAT IT IS NEVERTHELESS GOOD FOR:

  1. IT IS NOT A YMCA DOCUMENT. This project's evidence that Canadian YMCA
     camping begins in 1889 at Chance Harbour is internal -- the Montreal
     association's own News Bulletin of May 1944, and the 1989 centenary. Here
     the claim is carried in a federal statistical publication, tabled by a
     minister of the Crown. That is a different kind of record even if the
     text behind it came from the same place, and it puts the 1889 date in
     public print in 1940, four years before the News Bulletin list.
  2. IT DATES McEWEN'S NATIONAL OFFICE EARLIER THAN THIS PROJECT COULD. The
     Concordia file runs 1941-45 and Greig's quotation is 1945; the 1938-40
     survey has him in the post already.
  3. "PARTICULARLY CONCERNED WITH THE EDUCATIONAL ASPECTS OF CAMPING" is how
     the YMCA described its camping to the federal government, in a survey of
     schooling, in the decade Kanawana was running under McEwen's national
     office. It is a claim about what camps were FOR.

=====================================================================
ONE MORE LINE, IN THE 1943-44 SURVEY'S INDEX OF PERIODICAL ARTICLES
=====================================================================

  "McEwen, Nelson.--Y.M.C.A. Boys work as it relates to schools. N.H.S.B.
  March, 4-5."

AN ARTICLE BY McEWEN THIS PROJECT DOES NOT HOLD. N.H.S.B. is not expanded
anywhere the abbreviation key could be found in this scan; every other
N.H.S.B. citation in the index is on home-and-school subjects ("Home and
school ideas gathered from a trans-Canada tour", "A new programme for The
Home and School"), so it is very probably the NATIONAL HOME AND SCHOOL
BULLETIN of the Canadian Home and School and Parent-Teacher Federation.
THAT IS AN INFERENCE FROM NEIGHBOURING ENTRIES AND IS NOT ASSERTED. The year
is not given either -- only "March, 4-5" -- and the survey it indexes covers
1943-44.

"Kanawana" does not occur anywhere in the 4 MB of text. Checked.
